recent_posts.title: An AI agent coding skeptic tries AI agent coding, in excessive detail
recent_posts.summary: A self-described AI agent skeptic documents their journey from dismissing agentic coding to becoming a cautious convert after working with Claude Opus 4.5 and OpenAI Codex. The author shares detailed real-world experiments: building a YouTube scraper, a FastAPI webapp, Rust packages with Python bindings (icon rendering, word clouds, a terminal MIDI DAW, a physics simulator), and ultimately developing high-performance Rust implementations of ML algorithms (UMAP, HDBSCAN, GBDT) that outperform existing C/C++ libraries by 2-100x. Key insights include the importance of a well-crafted AGENTS.md file for controlling agent behavior, chaining Codex and Opus for iterative optimization, and the value of having approximate domain knowledge to audit agent output. The author remains measured—acknowledging real productivity gains while resisting hype—and open-sources all projects.

recent_posts.title: Comparing Nano Banana and Nano Banana Pro for AI image generation
recent_posts.summary: Nano Banana Pro (Gemini 3 Pro-based image generator) offers significant improvements over base Nano Banana including 2K/4K resolution, better typography, code rendering, and style transfer capabilities. However, it costs 3x more, has slower generation times due to mandatory thinking steps, and tends to push outputs toward realism which can undermine surreal or absurd prompts. The model excels at complex constraint adherence, grid generation, and grounding with Google Search for factual infographics, but may not always be the best choice depending on intended style. Base Nano Banana remains viable for many use cases where speed and cost matter more than maximum quality.

recent_posts.title: Nano Banana can be prompt engineered for extremely nuanced AI image generation
recent_posts.summary: Explores Google's Gemini 2.5 Flash Image (Nano Banana), an autoregressive image generation model with exceptional prompt adherence capabilities. Through extensive testing with complex, multi-constraint prompts, the author demonstrates how Nano Banana's 32,768-token context window and robust text encoder enable highly nuanced image generation, including multi-object editing, subject consistency without LoRAs, and structured input via JSON/HTML. The model excels at following detailed specifications but struggles with style transfer and has lenient content moderation. Includes practical examples, prompt engineering techniques, and a Python wrapper library for API access.

recent_posts.title: Claude 4.5 Haiku does not appreciate my attempts to jailbreak it
recent_posts.summary: An experiment testing jailbreak resistance across major LLMs reveals Claude 4.5 Haiku responds to adversarial prompts with unusually assertive, almost defensive language. While GPT-5-mini and Gemini 2.5 Flash can be jailbroken with moderate prompt engineering, Claude 4.5 Haiku explicitly recognizes jailbreak attempts and responds with passive-aggressive refusals that persist across multiple generations, suggesting Anthropic may have implemented a novel personality-based deterrent strategy.

recent_posts.title: Can modern LLMs actually count the number of b's in "blueberry"?
recent_posts.summary: A comprehensive test of modern LLMs reveals surprising inconsistencies in their ability to count letters in words. While most models correctly identify 3 r's in "strawberry" and 2 b's in "blueberry," GPT-5 Chat fails the blueberry test 73% of the time, often confidently claiming there are 3 b's. The study tested multiple models including GPT-5 variants, Claude, and Gemini across 274 trials, showing that tokenization limitations don't fully explain these failures since some models perform perfectly while others struggle with the same task.

recent_posts.title: LLMs can now identify public figures in images
recent_posts.summary: A comparative analysis reveals significant differences in how major LLMs handle public figure identification in images. While ChatGPT and Claude refuse to identify people due to privacy safeguards, Google's Gemini, Meta's Llama, Mistral, and Qwen readily identify public figures with varying accuracy. The research demonstrates that OpenAI and Anthropic have stricter RLHF training around privacy, but these restrictions can be bypassed through specific prompt engineering techniques. Gemini shows the highest accuracy in identification tasks, likely due to Google's extensive image training data from search operations.

recent_posts.title: Predicting Average IMDb Movie Ratings Using Text Embeddings of Movie Metadata
recent_posts.summary: A comprehensive exploration of using text embeddings to predict IMDb movie ratings, comparing traditional statistical models, neural networks, and training LLMs from scratch. The author processes IMDb datasets using Polars, generates embeddings with ModernBERT, and evaluates multiple modeling approaches including Support Vector Machines, MLPs, and custom transformer models. Results show that training a small LLM from scratch on raw JSON movie data achieved the best performance with an MSE of 1.026, outperforming both traditional models and pretrained embedding approaches.

recent_posts.title: As an Experienced LLM User, I Actually Don't Use Generative LLMs Often
recent_posts.summary: Despite being an experienced LLM user, Max Woolf doesn't use generative LLMs frequently due to various limitations but finds them useful for specific tasks. He discusses the nuances of prompt engineering, his professional work at BuzzFeed utilizing LLMs for specific projects, and reflects on their role in coding and writing. He highlights the importance of using LLMs responsibly and considers them as one of many tools in his tech arsenal.

recent_posts.title: The Best Way to Use Text Embeddings Portably is With Parquet and Polars
recent_posts.summary: Text embeddings, representing words and documents, are highly useful in various applications. While vector databases like faiss or Pinecone are typically used for handling embeddings, simpler methods involving numpy and formats like Parquet files can be more efficient for smaller projects. Parquet files, in combination with polars, offer a powerful alternative for storing embeddings and performing similarity searches with added metadata flexibility.

recent_posts.title: Can iterative prompting improve code quality with LLMs?
recent_posts.summary: The post explores the concept of iteratively improving code quality using LLMs like Claude 3.5 Sonnet by repeatedly asking the model to 'write better code.' Initial results of using basic prompts to refine a Python code sample show significant performance improvements, demonstrating an iterative speedup from a baseline of 657 milliseconds to code that runs in about 6 milliseconds after several iterations. Further experiments using prompt engineering, which explicitly guide the LLM with detailed instructions, yield even more optimized code. However, the process also reveals the limitations of LLMs, highlighting the necessity for human oversight to ensure correctness and manage subtle bugs.

top_posts.title: AI Seinfeld was the peak of AI-generated content. It will never happen again.
top_posts.summary: AI Seinfeld, an AI-generated sitcom parodying Seinfeld, went viral in early 2023 due to its unique combination of generative AI humor and nostalgic appeal. Using GPT-3 for scripting and Azure's speech synthesis APIs for voices, it captured the essence of Seinfeld's style. However, it faced significant challenges, including technical limitations and societal backlash, eventually leading to its decline after a controversial incident. Despite advancements in AI, the potential for creating a similar viral hit faces numerous hurdles, from ethical concerns to the complexities of maintaining engaging, automated content.

top_posts.title: Exploring GPT-4o's Advanced Voice Generation Capabilities Through Prompt Engineering
top_posts.summary: OpenAI's GPT-4o model showcases impressive advancements in AI voice generation through prompt engineering. Unlike existing text-to-speech models, GPT-4o can seamlessly alter its vocal style based on user prompts without requiring specific training for each style. Although the technology displays potential to revolutionize voice acting, its high cost and current limitations, such as the availability of only three distinct voices, pose challenges. Additionally, ethical concerns around voice impersonation highlight the need for cautious use.
